# BOOK 1 of 2: "The Pomp of Yesterday" by Joseph Hocking (Gutenberg 25136)

**Front matter:** Title page; Kipling epigraph "Recessional" (Lest We Forget). Publisher Hodder and Stoughton, London/New York/Toronto. Extract from General Sir William Robertson, March 2, 1918: "...measure of our ultimate success... strength with which we put our religious convictions into our action..."

**Foreword (Author, March 1918):** Four years of war; "Why is Victory delayed?" is the book's question. Statements about drink/nation "related to him by those in a position to know." Somme descriptions from transcripts of experiences. Author visited front again (Thiepval, Goomecourt, La Boiselle, Contalmaison). Finished writing August 1917; Russia chaos anticipated.

**Chapter list (42 chapters):** I The Man Without a Past; II Sir Roger Granville's Suggestion; III The Strange Behaviour of George St. Mabyn; IV I Meet Captain Springfield; V How a Man Worked a Miracle; VI Paul Edgecumbe's Memory; VII A Cause of Failure; VIII I Become an Eavesdropper; IX Edgecumbe is Missing; X The Struggle in the Trenches; XI Edgecumbe's Story; XII The Struggle on the Somme; XIII Edgecumbe's Madness; XIV Edgecumbe's Logic; XV Devonshire; XVI Lorna Bolivick's Home; XVII A New Development; XVIII A Tragic Happening; XIX A Mysterious Illness; XX A Strange Night; XXI Colonel McClure's Verdict; XXII Edgecumbe's Resolve; XXIII Springfield's Progress; XXIV A Strange Love-Making; XXV 'Why is Victory Delayed?'; XXVI 'Where Does God Come In?'; XXVII Seeing London; XXVIII Sunshine and Shadow; XXIX Cross Currents; XXX The March of Events; XXXI Edgecumbe's Return; XXXII The Great Meeting; XXXIII The Lifted Curtain; XXXIV Memory; XXXV Afterwards; XXXVI Edgecumbe's Resolution; XXXVII Maurice St. Mabyn; XXXVIII A Bombshell; XXXIX Springfield at Bay; XL Maurice St. Mabyn's Generosity; XLI The New Hope; XLII An Unfinished Story.

**Narrator:** Captain Luscombe (Cornish; ex-Volunteer officer, recruiter, later battalion officer; ~39, rowing blue, 12 st, 6 ft). Writes from 1917.

**Main characters:**
- **Paul Edgecumbe** (amnesiac; named by Luscombe after Mount Edgecumbe and St Paul; real name Jack Carbis, son of Lord Carbis, brewer/distiller peer; Maurice's line). Met Plymouth Harbour, spring 1915, from Bombay, half-naked, L5 notes in vest; enlisted at Plymouth recruiting meeting (D.C.L.I.). Rescued Luscombe from German dugout by talking 30 Germans into surrender (ch V). Later private, then artillery officer, Major, D.S.O.; converted at Y.M.C.A. hut in France; preaches total abstinence, anti-drink, "God's war." Missing after night at Luscombe's billet (Ottermouth area? no—St. Pinto/St. Pierre); found in Somme (Montauban area) digging out Springfield. Taken to Bolivick (Devon); falls ill (poisoned, blue mark on left arm below elbow, Indian poison injection); saved by Colonel McClure (Plymouth St George's Military Hospital, Indian experience). Memory returns at Bolivick dinner when parents Lord & Lady Carbis arrive ("Jack!"). Engaged-in-principle to Lorna; Lorna finally accepts. Father's name John; mother Lady Carbis.
- **Lorna Bolivick** (~19-20; daughter of Sir Thomas Bolivick, Bolivick house near South Petherwin, Devon, five miles off; mother Lady Bolivick; brothers at front incl. Tom; nurse/V.A.D.). Named after Lorna Doone. Gave Luscombe a promise written in diary dated May 29 (1916), witnessed "Lorna Bolivick, Bolivick, South Petherwin." Feels snake-like fascination with Springfield; secretly believed his lies about Edgecumbe; engaged/understanding with Springfield; later with Jack Carbis.
- **Captain Horace Springfield** (30–35; tall, dark, thin, receding forehead, scar on right cheek below temple/under right ear; "snakes" per Lorna and Norah). Egypt/India; Indian cry "vengeance." Killed/tried to kill Maurice St. Mabyn (Egypt, April 1914 story; stabbed him, left him, attacked him near Bizna in July 1914 with others). Lied about Maurice's death to Devon; conspired with George St. Mabyn. Buried under rubble by Edgecumbe at Somme (July 1916). Later Colonel, Carbis heir ambitions. Attempted to poison Edgecumbe at Bolivick (fell ill). Suicide by injected Indian poison in Plymouth hotel after exposure (ch XXXVIII–XL).
- **George St. Mabyn** (~28; Major; brother of Maurice; estate Granitelands/St Mabyn house; engaged to Norah Blackwater; complicit with Springfield; haunted, drinks). 
- **Maurice St. Mabyn** (brother; "killed" in Egypt; actually alive, prisoner among Turks 6 months, released after Baghdad; returned to Devon in Ch XXXVIII).
- **Norah Blackwater** (~25, tall stylish; engaged to Maurice, then George).
- **Sir Roger Granville** (chairman at Plymouth meeting; Granitelands; Lady Granville); **Colonel Gray** (Exeter; Edgecumbe's colonel later).
- **Sir Thomas Bolivick** (stout, florid, hearty; wants Springfield as heir; later favours Carbis).
- **Colonel Heywood** (OTC CO; says Edgecumbe is an artillery officer with genius).
- **Colonel McClure** (Scottish; Army doctor, 12 years India; St George's Military Hospital Plymouth).
- **Dr. Merril** (South Petherwin doctor).
- **Charlie Buller** (~24; first lieutenant Devonshire Yeomanry; wounded; suitor to Lorna; wrists weak; under Springfield's influence).
- **Vernon Mallory** (ex-Foreign Office, retired; sharp; wife Margaret, blind; daughter **Enid Mallory** ("Pussy") and Reggie Beauchamp, engaged).
- **Lieutenant Reginald "Reggie" Beauchamp** (RN; commands destroyer *Snipe*; mother Mrs. Beauchamp, Lorne Villas, widow of Admiral).
- **Travers Nugent** (~40s, Jermyn Street, cottage "The Hut" at Ottermouth; lives on wits; fair moustache, cold blue eyes; butler **Sinnett**; chauffeur **Dixon**; "avuncular oof-bird" uncle).
- **Bhagwan Singh**, Maharajah of Sindkhote (Eastern prince; wanted Violet Maynard; offered £20,000 to Nugent; cruel).
- **Leslie Chermside** (ex-24th Lancers; Indian debts; hired by Maharajah to woo Violet; fell in love; confessed to Mallory; fled on *Cobra*; murder suspicion).
- **Levi Levison** (Jewish "financial agent"/pawnbroker's assistant; bought Chermside's debts; murdered on marsh, Ottermouth, ~Wed night; body in pool under railway embankment, throat cut, stabbed in back).
- **Pierre Legros** (French onion-seller, Breton; ex-lover of Louise; killed Levison, confesses; suicide in Nugent's dining room).
- **Louise Aubin** (Violet's French maid; from Dicamp, Normandy/Brittany; flirts with Levison and Nugent; later engaged to Lazarus Lowch).
- **Montague Maynard** (Birmingham screw-manufacturer, Harborne; Park Lane; Manor House Ottermouth; loud jolly).
- **Violet Maynard** (~25 daughter; beautiful; Academy picture; refused Bhagwan Singh at Brabazon House ball).
- **Aunt Sarah Dymmock** (tiny old spinster, Violet's great-aunt; shrewd; gave Chermside securities £250,000).
- **Captain Simon Brant** (yellow, dwarfish skipper of steam yacht *Cobra*; crew of toughs; "sleeping snake").
- **Bully Cheeseman** (bullet-headed mate); **Wiley** (second mate).
- **Nettle Jimpson** (draper's assistant, Grigg & Winter's, Weymouth; fiancé Ned Parsons, acting gunner of *Snipe*; forced aboard *Cobra* as stewardess; threw cinders into engines).
- **Bill Tuke** ("The Bootlace Man"; Nugent's henchman; locked Enid in grotto).
- **Lazarus Lowch** (busybody; jury foreman).
- **Sergeant Bruce** (Ottermouth police).
- **Enid, Reggie, Mrs Beauchamp**; **Mona Dartring** (Enid's friend).

**Book 1 plot summary (key events in order):**
1. Plymouth harbour meeting, spring 1915: Luscombe meets amnesiac man; names him Paul Edgecumbe; recruiting speech; Edgecumbe enlists.
2. Sir Roger Granville, Granitelands; Lorna Bolivick and Norah Blackwater; George St. Mabyn's strange behaviour; Lorna's promise (diary, May 29).
3. Luscombe visits St Mabyn's house; meets Springfield; Springfield says Maurice died in Egypt.
4. France 1915–16: Edgecumbe rescues Luscombe at dugout (miracle of persuading 30 Germans). Edgecumbe's warnings about drink and God's neglect.
5. Luscombe overhears George & Springfield plotting to kill Edgecumbe (copse near St Pinto). Edgecumbe vanishes after pistol shot.
6. Somme, July 1916: Edgecumbe rescues Luscombe and digs out Springfield. Edgecumbe converted (Y.M.C.A. hut), speaks of God, drink.
7. Devonshire visit (Bolivick): Edgecumbe falls for Lorna; poisoned; McClure saves him (blue mark on arm). Springfield and Buller present.
8. London 1917: Edgecumbe studies London, House of Commons, Cabinet minister; "Where does God come in?" Springfield pursues Lorna.
9. Edgecumbe commissioned, D.S.O., publicly speaks at London meeting; parents arrive at Bolivick, memory returns ("Jack").
10. Maurice St. Mabyn appears; Springfield exposed; Springfield asks Lorna to marry him; Maurice confronts; Springfield leaves.
11. Springfield later found dead (poison) in Plymouth. Lorna's secret: Springfield threatened Jack's exposure; she promised to marry him. Jack and Lorna engaged; Luscombe is best man-type.

(Book 1 ends with Luscombe telling Lorna and Jack's engagement; Jack to "beard the lion" Sir Thomas.)

# BOOK 2 of 2: "A Traitor's Wooing" by Headon Hill (Gutenberg 33453; illustrated, Ward Lock 1909)

**Front matter:** Author's other titles (The Avengers, Millions of Mischief, Her Splendid Sin, Unmasked at Last, A Race with Ruin, The Hidden Victim, Radford Shone). Frontispiece: Violet "Is that all you have to say to me?" asked Violet quietly.

**Chapter list:** I Two Villains and the Heroine; II "A Screw Loose Somewhere"; III Presage of Storm; IV Nugent Moves a Pawn; V Under the Searchlight; VI The Cry from the Train; VII The Face in the Pool; VIII Intercepted; IX The Inquisitive Foreman; X The Lure of Love; XI The Peering Eyes; XII The *Cobra's* Sailing Orders; XIII Fool's Paradise Lost; XIV The Creaking Stair; XV A Council of Three; XVI Barbed Shafts; XVII "The Bootlace Man"; XVIII The Trap is Set; XIX The Sleeping Snake; XX Blue Light and Green; XXI The Trap Closes; XXII The Shadow of Horror; XXIII In the Stone Grotto; XXIV In the Toils; XXV The Last Chance Fails; XXVI Enid is "Mixed Up"; XXVII Pursuit; XXVIII Travers Nugent Pays; XXIX The Sting of the Nettle; XXX Aftermath of Storm.

**Main characters:**
- **Travers Nugent**: well-built, middle-aged, long fair moustache, close-set blue eyes, lives on wits in Jermyn Street flat; rents The Hut at Ottermouth (South Devon) — manservant Sinnett (sphinx-like), chauffeur Dixon (Darracq car). Hired by Maharajah.
- **Bhagwan Singh**, Maharajah of Sindkhote (jewelled turban, black moustache, cruel); proposed to Violet at Brabazon House ball; rejected, laughed at. Plans abduction; pays £20,000 on delivery to Sindkhote (Runn of Cutch, India). Owns steamer *Cobra* (turbine yacht, 2,000 tons, chartered at Weymouth/Portland).
- **Leslie Chermside**: ex-24th Lancers, Indian debts bought by Levison; cashiered after embezzlement-like lapse; tall, bronzed; falls in love with Violet; confesses to Mallory/Violet; flees; captured on *Cobra*; chained in lower-deck cell.
- **Violet Maynard**: tall, beautiful, daughter of Montague Maynard (stout florid, 60, screw-maker, Harborne/Birmingham; Park Lane; rents Ottermouth Manor House from noble owner). Mother dead. Great-aunt **Sarah (Aunt Sarah) Dymmock** (tiny, sharp, grey curls, lace cap, sunshade; wealthy; gave Chermside securities worth ~£250,000 transfer; said "the elements propitious").
- **Levi Levison**: Jewish "financial agent"/pawnbroker's assistant, lisps, dark eyes; murdered on marsh (Ottermouth), body in pool under railway embankment, throat cut, stabbed three times in back and once in chest. Lodged at the Plume Hotel.
- **Pierre Legros**: French onion-seller (Breton; from Dicamp); lugger from Exmouth; blue jean; jealous of Louise; killed Levison; confessed; suicide with knife in Nugent's room.
- **Louise Aubin**: French maid (Violet's), vain, flirtatious, calculating; told Nugent about Chermside's marsh appointment; later engaged to Lazarus Lowch.
- **Vernon Mallory**: ex-Foreign Office, 40 years; keen eyes; wife Margaret (blind); daughter **Enid Mallory** ("Pussy", ~19); Enid engaged to Reggie Beauchamp (Lieutenant RN, commands destroyer *Snipe*, Plymouth; mother Mrs Beauchamp, widow of Admiral, Lorne Villas).
- **Lazarus Lowch**: lean, cadaverous, nosy busybody; spies through privet hedge; jury foreman at Levison inquest.
- **General Kruse** ("widow's Kruse", drinker, rubicund, voice like thunder).
- **Sergeant Bruce**: Ottermouth police.
- **Simon Brant**: captain of *Cobra*, dwarf with pear-shaped head, yellow complexion, hissing breath, wheezy treble, Derringer; killed Black Jake (fireman) and cremated him; threw Derringer overboard.
- **Bully Cheeseman**: bullet-headed mate; once suspected of being Jack the Ripper; slapped by Nettle.
- **Nettle Jimpson**: tall, powerful draper's assistant (Grigg & Winter's, Weymouth), fiancé Ned Parsons (acting gunner, *Snipe*); shipped aboard *Cobra*; dumped bucket of cinders into engine.
- **Bill Tuke** ("The Bootlace Man"): Nugent's underling; onion-sack/bootlace hawker; in Chermside's Weymouth/*Cobra* job; locked Enid in grotto.
- **Violet's servant Watson** (butler).
- **Mrs Mallory**, **Mona Dartring**, **Dr** (unnamed); Ottermouth Club members: Vernon Mallory, Reggie, General Kruse, Nugent, Chermside.

**Key events in order (Book 2):**
1. Ch I: Brabazon House ball; Maharajah approaches Violet; Nugent in charge; Violet refused and mocked Bhagwan; plot: Chermside (Indian debts, ex-Lancer, now guard of Maharajah) to win Violet; elopement on yacht; Nugent to get £20,000 when she sets foot in Sindkhote.
2. Ch II: Ottermouth described (Flagstaff Hill, marsh, old river mouth, club). Mallory and Reggie discuss Chermside at club window. Chermside meets Levison on marsh footpath (Levison: "I've bought up your Indian debts"; "Wednesday night at ten o'clock" ultimatum).
3. Ch III: Manor House; Aunt Sarah drives onion-seller away at point of sunshade; Nugent lunches; Chermside tells Nugent "I am not going on with the damned thing!"; Aunt Sarah says "Travers Nugent... wouldn't trust him with a shilling."
4. Ch IV: Nugent sends servant Sinnett to fetch Pierre Legros; Nugent meets Levison; Enid Mallory with Reggie at seafront; Louise Aubin's lover conflict.
5. Ch V: Reggie and Enid on marsh; they hear cry; Chermside passes in searchlight beam from cruiser *Terrible*; "face" rays; they hide in "ambush" glade.
6. Ch VI: Picnic-tea (Violet's); train passenger yells "the face in the pool" (Violet hears "the face in the pool").
7. Ch VII: Vernon Mallory finds body (throat cut) in pool under embankment; Reggie identifies Levison from club window.
8. Ch VIII: Louise meets Nugent on road; claims Levison's murderer is Pierre Legros; Nugent diverts her by naming Chermside (secret meeting).
9. Ch IX: Inquest at Plume Hotel; Lowch foreman; Chermside testifies; Reggie questioned about cry; Lowch spies from hedge.
10. Ch X: Chermside and Violet in rose garden declare love.
11. Ch XI: Louise spies lovers; reports to Nugent at The Hut; Pierre Legros hiding at window; Nugent sends Louise away; Pierre leaves ("Poor Pierre! He will have to strike").
12. Ch XII: Nugent visits Weymouth, meets Brant on *Cobra* ("Advance" signal plan; blue light then green at Colebrook/Coldbrook Chine, half mile west of town).
13. Ch XIII: Mallory confronts Chermside about wealth; Aunt Sarah sails boat, gives Chermside securities (~£250,000); Nugent drags Chermside into club.
14. Ch XIV: Nugent in card-room tells Chermside he is suspect; plan: flee on *Cobra*; creaking stair; billiard-room trio (Mallory, General Kruse, Lowch).
15. Ch XV: Mallory and Reggie/Enid council; Mallory suspects Nugent; "bootlace man" seen.
16. Ch XVI: Louise tells Violet Chermside met Levison; Violet confronts Nugent; orangery scene with Chermside, who refuses explanation.
17. Ch XVII: Enid investigates The Hut; locked in stone grotto by Tuke ("The Bootlace Man").
18. Ch XVIII: Nugent tricks Violet, says Chermside fleeing; sets rendezvous at Colebrook Chine at eleven; Violet goes.
19. Ch XIX: Brant gets letter; hires Nettle Jimpson as stewardess; *Cobra* leaves Weymouth; Nettle promised Plymouth stop (lie).
20. Ch XX: Chermside at The Hut; Tuke signals blue and green flares at chine; launch comes.
21. Ch XXI: Violet arrives at beach; Tuke says Chermside went to steamer; Violet taken by launch to *Cobra*.
22. Ch XXII: Chermside boards *Cobra* (by second launch trip); fights launch crew; knocked out; chained in hold. Nettle meets Chermside on deck.
23. Ch XXIII: Enid locked in grotto; finds Pierre Legros hidden under matting; Pierre cuts roof open; Enid escapes but misses Violet's voice.
24. Ch XXIV: Violet on *Cobra*; Brant reveals Sindkhote plot; Nettle befriends Violet.
25. Ch XXV: Nettle finds Chermside chained in black hole, gives water; Brant refuses Plymouth stop.
26. Ch XXVI: Mallory and Lowch in club; Lowch's accusation about Enid; Enid escapes, reports; telephone exchange.
27. Ch XXVII: Reggie receives phone call from Enid; takes *Snipe* out; chases *Cobra*; *Cobra* escapes at 40 knots.
28. Ch XXVIII: Nugent returns to The Hut; Mallory and Sergeant Bruce arrive; Pierre appears from behind screen, confesses killing Levison; Pierre stabs Nugent, then himself.
29. Ch XXIX: Nettle sabotages *Cobra* engines with cinders; *Snipe* catches; Brant threatens Nettle; *Cobra* disabled.
30. Ch XXX: Aftermath: Chermside has confessed to Mallory; Montague Maynard accepts him; Maynard buys Grigg & Winter's for Nettle; Lowch engaged to Louise; Aunt Sarah; "THE END".

(Ward, Lock & Co. advertisement pages follow for other titles.)
